key_insight: V-PaSS uses physics-aware alloy and device representations to better predict perovskite solar-cell performance for unfamiliar materials and architectures.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help screen new absorber alloys and device stacks without requiring a pre-solved crystal structure for every composition.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, cell polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
evidence_signal: On an institution-grouped evaluation with unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with reported error reductions of 15.7–19.0% on unseen absorber alloys.
watch_item: Extrapolation remains dependent on the 23-endpoint representation and its interpolation assumptions; the abstract does not establish reliability outside that chemistry space.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
